paragraphs: Gulliver's Travels is a famous book by Jonathan Swift. It is 300 years old this year.
On Sunday, people in Cavan had a big party for the book. Swift wrote a lot of it in Cavan. He stayed with his friend Thomas Sheridan at a house called Quilca House.
There were games, stories and plays for families. At 5pm, a giant made of light woke up at Urney Church. It was a lantern six metres tall. An orchestra and singers played music across the street.
Later, more than 100 handmade lanterns went through the town in a parade. People walked with them in the dark.
Cavan has celebrated 300 years of Gulliver's Travels, the famous book by Jonathan Swift. The event, called Gulliver 300, took place on Sunday.

Swift wrote much of the story in Mullagh, Co Cavan, while he was staying with his friend Thomas Sheridan at Quilca House. The county's arts officer, Karina Charles-Lynch, said the day was a way to remember this link.

Families could enjoy workshops, a theatre group and traditional storytelling. The main event started at 5pm, when a huge lantern of a "sleeping giant", 20 feet tall, was lit at Urney Church. The Cavan Sinfonia Orchestra and local singers performed at the courthouse across the street.

A short film based on the book was shown on the front of the courthouse. Then more than 100 handmade lanterns were carried through the town in a "dark skies" parade. The day was part of Eco Féile, Cavan's new festival about the environment, and many families stayed until late in the evening.
Co Cavan has marked the 300th anniversary of Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels with a day of events celebrating the county's close connection to the classic satire.

According to Cavan County Council arts officer Karina Charles-Lynch, Swift wrote much of the book in Mullagh while staying with his friend Thomas Sheridan at Quilca House. She said the Gulliver 300 celebration was a chance to honour that legacy.

Throughout Sunday, visitors could take part in interactive workshops, watch a theatre ensemble and listen to folklore storytelling. The highlight came at 5pm, when a 20-foot lantern sculpture of a "sleeping giant" was illuminated at Urney Church, accompanied by the Cavan Sinfonia Orchestra and local singers performing at the courthouse opposite.

A short film inspired by the novel was projected onto the courthouse facade, before more than 100 handcrafted lanterns were carried through the town in a "dark skies" parade. The event was held in partnership with Eco Féile, Cavan's new sustainability festival.
Co Cavan has commemorated the tercentenary of Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels, staging a day of festivities that underlined the county's intimate ties to the celebrated satire.

Cavan County Council arts officer Karina Charles-Lynch noted that Swift penned much of the work in Mullagh while lodging with his friend Thomas Sheridan at Quilca House, and described Gulliver 300 as a tribute to that literary heritage.

Sunday's programme featured interactive workshops, a theatrical ensemble and folklore storytelling. The centrepiece, unveiled at dusk, was a towering 20-foot lantern sculpture of a slumbering giant, illuminated at Urney Church to the strains of the Cavan Sinfonia Orchestra and local choristers stationed at the courthouse opposite.
